 Tottenham’s Luca Williams-Barnett told not to let English football change him
 Sport 
 By PA News Agency 
 Share
 Luca Williams-Barnett has made three appearances this season (John Walton/PA) 
 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
 and has been written by our American colleagues.
 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 Tottenham academy starlet Luca Williams-Barnett has been told not to let English football change him ahead of a potential full debut on Saturday.
 Williams-Barnett only turned 18 last month, but has produced telling contributions in two cameos in recent Premier League matches with Crystal Palace and Leeds.
 With Roberto De Zerbi short of options at left wing due to injuries ahead of Saturday’s visit of Ipswich, the Italian could turn to Williams-Barnett, who has been described as a “special talent” by the Spurs boss.
 Almost a mesmerising assist on debut for Luca Williams-Barnett 🪄 @SpursOfficial pic.twitter.com/ntDNIyMez7 
 — Premier League (@premierleague) October 31, 2026 
 Ex-Tottenham midfielder Micky Hazard played with one of the north London club’s greatest ever homegrown players in Glenn Hoddle during a trophy-laden spell in the 1980s.
 Back in August, De Zerbi invited 22 former players for lunch with his staff and first-team squad at Hotspur Way and Hazard quickly made a beeline for Williams-Barnett given the growing excitement about the teenager in recent years.
 “I am a great believer in producing your own,” Hazard, co-founder of mental health charity Legend on the Bench, told the Press Association. “What the homegrown do is they give the club its heart and soul because they know the importance of the club because they’ve come through the system.
 “When we talk about that we haven’t produced a real superstar since Harry Kane, I have to be honest with you and say we have one in the making now. I think Luca’s going to be something incredibly special.
 “And the sooner we get him in that team, we can give him a chance to grow and develop because he’s got the lot from what I’ve seen of him.
 “I spoke to him at the dinner, I sat next to him and I said to him, ‘look Luca, please, all I ask of you, you’re such a special talent and don’t let English football change you’, because I said, ‘add to your game, add some of the things that they want you to add, but don’t let them change you’.
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Luca Williams-Barnett (@luca_lb10) 
 “I said, ‘don’t let them take away that flair, that genius and that creativity because that’s you and that’s who you are and that’s who you are going to be. You’re going to be in the Glenn Hoddle mould, the fans are going to idolise and worship you, but if you change and become this up and down, run around and tackle, and lose that natural instinct you have, it will only be you to blame’.
 “Glenn went through the same process where managers tried to add this and that or take away this and that, but he was strong enough mentally to stick to his game and look at the worship he has experienced.
 “Luca could be the next… different to Glenn Hoddle, but that mould because he is very special.”
 A Legend on the Bench park bench outside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium was unveiled in September and Hazard wants more next to other Premier League and Football League clubs.
 Hazard, who set up Legend on the Bench after the death of nephew Jay in 2019 and has installed more than 100 benches, said: “It is a further step along the line of getting as many benches as we can into the public domain to help saves lives.
 “Spurs doing what they have done hopefully means other Premier League and Football League clubs will be interested in having these benches.”
